reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended The timeout does not cancel reverse-proxy database calls, transport-level regression coverage is missing, and the permit-release test can pass despite a semaphore leak.
3 open issues - [Propagate request context to reverse-proxy database calls](https://github.com/stackql/stackql/pull/906#discussion_r4504088693) · New - [Assert follow-up calls reach the backend after permit release](https://github.com/stackql/stackql/pull/906#discussion_r4504088704) · New - [Add black-box timeout and cancellation tests for both transports](https://github.com/stackql/stackql/pull/906#discussion_r4504088709) · New
What changed in this PR This PR adds shared MCP tool-call admission limits and request deadlines, addressing part of #828. HTTP server timeouts and body limits remain deferred. **Changes:** - Registers middleware that acquires semaphore permits and applies request deadlines to `tools/call`. - Defines non-positive settings as disabling the corresponding control, leaving other methods unchanged. - Adds in-process tests for concurrency limits, timeouts, permit recovery, and disabled limits. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `pkg/​mcp_server/​server.go` | Wires the limits middleware and shared semaphore into server construction. | | `pkg/​mcp_server/​limits.go` | Implements cancellation-aware admission, deadlines, and deferred permit release. | | `pkg/​mcp_server/​limits_test.go` | Adds blocking-backend tests for the configured controls. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: The timeout remains ineffective for the `reverse_proxy` backend: `ExecQuery` and `query` discard the context and use `db.Exec`/`db.Query` in `internal/stackql/mcpbackend/mcp_reverse_proxy_backend_service.go:75–76,110–111`. A stalled database call can therefore keep `next` and its semaphore permit occupied after the deadline. Use `ExecContext`/`QueryContext` with the request context, and check row-iteration errors so cancellation is not returned as partial success.

This permit-release test still passes if `defer sem.Release(1)` is removed. After the first call, later calls simply expire inside `Acquire` at the 50ms server deadline, well before their 2s client deadlines; ignoring the returned error makes that indistinguishable from reaching the backend. Assert that each call returns a backend timeout as a tool result rather than an admission/transport error, so a leaked permit fails the test.

The new admission and timeout behavior has only in-memory coverage with a cooperative backend, leaving deadline propagation and recovery through HTTP and stdio unverified. Add black-box scenarios in `test/robot/functional/mcp.robot` for overlapping slow calls, explicit cancellation of a queued waiter, and a successful follow-up request after timeout on both transports. These regressions are required by the repository's behavior-change testing guidelines.
